claims.text: The starting material is an as-received structural Ti-6Al-4V alloy with moderate surface hardness and wear resistance.
Plasma nitriding Ti-6Al-4V will form a hardened TiN diffusion layer at its surface.
Exposure to low-pressure NH3 at approximately 850°C for 6 hours followed by controlled cooling will produce a continuous, nanostructured TiN-rich layer.
The nitrided surface layer will consist primarily of TiN precipitates and interstitial nitrogen-enriched titanium phases.
Nitrogen introduced by plasma nitriding diffuses into the titanium-alloy surface.
Diffused nitrogen forms titanium nitride and solid-solution-strengthened surface regions.
Titanium nitride has sufficiently high hardness to resist contact-induced plastic deformation.
Increasing the hardness of a modified TC4/Ti-6Al-4V surface can improve its wear resistance.
The proposed TiN-rich layer will reduce both adhesive and abrasive wear.
Plasma-nitrided samples will have surface hardness approximately 20–50% higher than untreated Ti-6Al-4V.
Plasma-nitrided samples will have a lower wear rate than untreated Ti-6Al-4V under identical test conditions.
The expected improvement should hold at room temperature under moderate-load dry sliding at about 0.1 m/s over several hundred meters.
Ball-on-disk testing under the proposed conditions simulates service conditions for structural titanium components.
Very high temperatures or corrosive atmospheres may require different nitriding parameters or additional treatments.
The hardness and wear responses depend on nitriding time, nitriding temperature, and the starting alloy condition.
Nitriding may require optimization to avoid adversely affecting alloy ductility.
